newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek Magrizos denies involvement in share moves.
newsitem.headline: Greek Magrizos denies involvement in share moves.

text.p: Textile firm Magrizos, whose shares have been linked to an Athens brokerage default, said its shares' dramatic rise and fall over the past year may have been part of a "trading game" but denied any involvement.
"It could be that a trading game took place but we could neither intervene nor control it," David Magrizos, deputy managing director of Magrizos, told Reuters.

"Our family owns at least 70 percent of the firm as of today but we have no control over the free float which is 30 percent," he said, referring to that part of the share capital which is traded on the Athens bourse.
The Athens bourse has been closed for two days since Delta Securities, now charged with criminal fraud, failed to pay 2.6 billion drachmas to the exchange clearing house for Magrizos shares.
Magrizos traded at 201 drachmas a share on September 1 1995 and reached a high of 1,365 drachmas on September 13 this year before closing at 911 drachmas on November 7.
"We lacked the capacity to intervene even if we wanted to because this would have required large sums of money," said Magrizos.
He said Magrizos's major shareholders, who are all Magrizos' famility members, had nothing to with the episode.
Magrizos said he knew that Delta Securities and two or three more brokerages were actively trading his firm's shares.
"We knew that this brokerage was involved in trading our firm's shares," he told Reuters when asked if he was aware of the fact that Delta Securities acted as a market maker in his firm's shares.

He said he agreed with brokers who wanted the bourse closed while the mess is sorted out. The Athens bourse closed on Friday and failed to open on Monday as angry brokers were engaged in a lively debate over how to resolve the settlement fiasco.
"I absolutely agree. The brokers' stance is rational," said Magrizos.
"Settlement should take place in a short period of time and only cash or bank cheques not personal cheques should be accepted by the clearing house to avert a similar crisis in the future."
